text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* A corruption probe into alleged links between the Rome judiciary and building firms, involving some 25 people under official investigation, has reignited interest in Italy's faltering campaign to root out high-level corruption (all).

* Centre-right opposition parties on Wednesday blasted the government's border control policies and demanded a crackdown on illegal immigration following a spate of violent incidents involving foreigners (all).

* In an interview, centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said he did not trust separatist Northern League leader Umberto Bossi's political alliance for mayoral elections in Venice (Corriere della Sera).

* The Italian Treasury said the group of investors that will form a core of stable shareholders at telecoms operator Telecom Italia SpA should be in place by the end of September. The Treasury added that the general placement of Telecom shares aimed at institutional and retail investors was set for the second half of October (all).

* A report by national statistics institute Istat showed Italian producer prices rose 1.6 percent year-on-year in June against 1.1 percent in May. Istat report also showed wholesale prices fell 0.3 percent year-on-year in June against a 0.2 percent drop in May (all).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
